content:
1. What is the hosting provider?
  2. Do the messages in your spam folder have a red flame icon attached to them in the message list
  3. Most importantly what antivirus product do you use.

SPAM message processioning is relatively simple in Thunderbird and adheres to the information in the article you linked. That your experience is different is also not something I see as a suprise. Despite assertions to the contrary rarely do hosting providers not offer, and usually enforce, some sort of SPAM monitoring or exclusion. Your description of mail being returned to the spam folder after you make a manual decision is reminiscent to what happens at Yahoo. They constantly monitor all folders and just put the mail back in SPAM until such time as you buckle and upload your address book to their web site so their spam system can whitelist your contacts. An appalling situation, but most Yahoo customers just accept it.

Then we have the junk toolbars from a plethora of antivirus vendors that tell you they are protecting your from scams. but meddle well outside that area because they can. In the long term it usually makes Thunderbird unstable, but the third party antivirus product is "bullet proof". Interestingly Microsoft Defender scores well in virus detection/malware detection tests and does nothing with email at all. It is also not selling a subscription.

My guess if the change is happening in seconds as you say is local software. A mail server moving mail twice would not normally happen in seconds. A minute maybe but unlikely to be seconds. So I would start by pursuing any toolbars or offers to monitor scam in your antivirus product of choice.

Found a workaround solution via a long investigation with AI.

Requires entries in Config Editor: widget.non-native-theme.gtk.scrollbar.allow-buttons = true widget.gtk.overlay-scrollbars.enabled = false

Create a file ~/.config/gtk-3.0/gtk.css

Enter the following into the file: -GtkScrollbar-has-backward-stepper: true; -GtkScrollbar-has-forward-stepper: true;

The arrows are now back.
